name: scattered broken bricks and mortar lumps lying on a patch of red brick dust on the ground
label: wasteland_ruins/rubble-b

surfaces.part: rubble patch of broken bricks and brick dust

answer.evidence: The object is a flat ground decal, an irregular patch about 16px wide spanning rows 1-14. The width profile grows from 5 to 16 and shrinks to 12, so it is a blob with no vertical south face. The column scans show mixed brick, mortar and dust colours with no front-edge line, eave shadow or distinct front face. It is seen from above as a flat plate, which suits the flat kind, so it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny sprite of a few bricks, roughly 12x10 source pixels, on a transparent background. The references are full ground tiles (grass, cobble paving) that tile edge to edge, and the brief asks for a 4x3 tile ground patch. There is no continuous red brick dust surface under the bricks, so it is a small prop rather than a ground surface and does not match the kind. The measured facts look fine on their own: 14 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat coverage, and only 4% neutral dark edge pixels, which points to tinted brown-red outlines rather than black. The whole piece has only 14 colours, and the bricks are shaded with about 4 steps. That is shallower than the paving's per-stone shading and the grass's varied tufts. It also has none of the per-tile grain and speckle a ground patch needs. When in doubt, fail.
